THE PEOPLE BEHIND THE ARCHIVE

After the Landing

Our curiosity doesn’t end at touchdown.

We created Abandoned but not Forgotten for the NASA Space App Challenge, Peshawar. Our goal is to make the history of space exploration feel alive for the next generation.

This archive follows the hardware in our Moon and Mars catalogs: NASA missions alongside Soviet and Chinese explorers. Some are silent. Some still work. All have something to teach us.

FOLLOW THE EVIDENCE

Real hardware. Open sources.

Built from your 27-entry Moon catalog, 50-entry Mars catalog, and 77-entry NASA image reference list. Years and educational explanations supplement those catalogs. Each story links to official information and its image record.

About images, dates, and the catalog

Entries are not a count of unique objects: a rover and its instruments may appear separately; the Apollo 16 ultraviolet telescope appears under two names. Some photographs show a mission, an instrument assembly, a model, or an artist’s illustration rather than an isolated object on the surface. The image caption and NASA record identify what is shown.

Status reflects the supplied catalog, with historical clarifications. It is not live mission telemetry. Moon years show surface deployment ranges; Mars years show arrival. Active equipment should not be described as abandoned. Impact debris should not be treated as an intact lander.

The atmospheric reference-site background photographs are decorative. Hardware images come from NASA’s public image archive; individual records provide credits. NASA links do not imply NASA endorsement.

NASA-supported map locations

The Moon and Mars location directories cover all 77 catalog entries. Each site and hardware association links to NASA evidence. Landing references are distinguished from final rover locations; unknown, candidate and estimated object positions receive no confirmed coordinate pin.
